### Calendar
A month of days with their events, on a table the page renders.

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `css-only`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Example: A team schedule for October is a calendar. Choosing a delivery date in a form is the date picker.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Support: A seven-column month grid with weekday headers, today, days outside the month and event chips that ellipsize; week and day hourly grids with events placed by start and duration; a year of small months in as many columns as fit.

Web adaptation: A native table with a caption; the page renders the dates, navigation and events.

Known boundary: Events that overlap in time overlap on screen in the week and day views; the page splits them.

Full parity remains unassessed. Review provenance and specification links: [capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#calendar).

#### Contract

A month, week or day of events, or a year of months, on tables the page renders.

A `table.calendar` has a `<caption>` naming the month, a header row of weekday `<th scope="col">` cells, then a row per week. Each day `<td>` starts with a `<time datetime>` and may hold a `.calendar-events` list of links or text. Mark days from other months with `outside` and today with `aria-current="date"`. The page owns the dates, the navigation between months and the events; CSS draws seven equal columns, the today mark and event chips that ellipsize. On a phone the days get shorter and chips tighter. CSS only; there is no JavaScript. Use the date picker to choose a date for a field.

#### Syntax

```html
<table class="calendar">
  <caption>October 2026</caption>
  <thead>
    <tr><th scope="col"><abbr title="Sunday">Sun</abbr></th>…</tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td class="outside"><time datetime="2026-09-27">27</time></td>
      <td aria-current="date">
        <time datetime="2026-10-15">15</time>
        <ul class="calendar-events"><li><a href="/events/standup">Standup</a></li></ul>
      </td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

#### Rules

- `calendar-is-a-table`: Write .calendar as a <table> with a <caption> and a header row of weekdays. A grid of divs loses the day-to-weekday relationship.
- `calendar-has-a-caption`: Give the calendar a <caption> naming the month, such as "October 2026". Without it nothing says which month the days belong to.
